# Environment notes for this session (generated by launch.sh; not part of the research instructions)

These are facts about this machine that you cannot infer from the repo. The research instructions are in `program.md`.

- **Where you are.** This directory is a git worktree whose base branch is `autoresearch/master`. Work only here.
- **Python.** `$PY` is set to the shared interpreter (`/Volumes/memit/llm-database-poc-mirror/arhugula-persistent-memory/.claude/worktrees/c10k-route-a/.venv/bin/python`). Use it for every Python command. Never run `uv sync`, `pip install` or anything else that changes that environment.
- **One GPU.** The Mac has one Apple GPU with 48 GB of unified memory. Run one experiment at a time: before starting a run, `pgrep -f "edit.py"` must print nothing.
- **Long runs.** Your shell tool stops any single command after 10 minutes, and a run takes 30–70 minutes. So start each run in the background (the Bash tool's `run_in_background`), then wait in bounded steps of under 10 minutes and repeat until the run has finished, for example `for i in $(seq 1 50); do pgrep -f "edit.py" > /dev/null || break; sleep 10; done`. Do NOT wait with an unbounded loop such as `while pgrep -f edit.py; do sleep 30; done`: the call is cut off at 10 minutes and you lose track of the run.
- **Shell aliases.** `cat`, `ls`, `grep`, `find` and `du` are aliased to other tools on this machine. Write `command cat`, `command grep`, `command ls`, and so on, to get the standard ones. Use `/usr/bin/git` for git.
- **Git.** Commit each experiment on your branch before running it, and reset on discard (`/usr/bin/git reset --hard HEAD~1`). `results.tsv`, `run.log`, `runs/` and `SUMMARY.md` are ignored by git, so resets leave them in place. The repository's commit hooks are switched off for this session.
- **The human.** The human is here for setup and answers your setup confirmation. After that, nobody will reply until the human comes back.
